content: I warlock tank in classic.  I have two different talent builds that I use, depending on if I want extra mitigation or extra threat. content:
Personally, I would like to see demonology become warlock tanking spec. Hear me out:

1. There already is a precedent for warlock tanking (Twin Emperors)
2. Demonology has a lot of hidden tanking synergies - Demonic Embrace gives you more stamina, Demonic Aegis gives you more armor, DSing voidwalker restores 3% total health every 4 seconds, Master Demonologist with voidwalker out reduces physical damage taken by 10%, Soul Link transfers 30% of damage taken to your controlled demon (probably voidwalker for tanking). Granted, you cant use both DS and SL at the same time
3. Searing Pain causes a high amount of threat and is ideal for single target tanking
4. Cloth items that are designed to make you more tanky already exist in the game - like https://database.turtle-wow.org/?itemset=520, which gives you a lot of armor and has +armor set bonus
5. Currently warlocks have 3 dps specs. Balancing a class with three dps specs is clearly very hard if not impossible, while balancing a class with only two dps specs would be much easier. Besides, who wouldnt want more tanks?
6. This spec can also be combined with the currently underwhelming fire warlock theme since it utilises Searing Pain and possibly Hellfire for aoe threat

Here is a sample talent build with the current talent trees:
https://talents.turtle-wow.org/warlock/0-CUI1LH1V-550UCI

We grab Intensity to resist pushback while casting Searing Pain, we have 11% crit chance on Searing Pain just from talents, we take all tanking talents from Demonology and Fel Domination/Master Summoner to instantly summon a new voidwalker to eat 30% damage in case first one dies

author: Bellegar
content:
Things to keep in mind:
- Fear, in vanilla, has heartbeat resists (every second there's a chance for it to break on its own, which increases with every tick), so most of the time it'll not last longer than 14-16 seconds anyway.
- Damage can break it and there's a damage threshold (a certain amount of damage that needs to be done in a short amount of time) that will cause Fear to be removed.
- Instant damage generally has a higher chance to break Fear, so if you're with a friend that's shooting at it or if your imp does Firebolt, it has a higher chance to break.
- If you're in a tight space and the mob runs towards a pack you don't wanna pull, you can use Curse of Recklessness to make it temporarily ignore the Fear; then apply another curse when it gets closer to you.
- Last, but not least, when you cast Fear the mob will generally run away from you, so if you want to use it in dungeons you should position yourself on the other side of the pack in order to guide it towards the back. Also, this means you should generally not run away after it when solo'ing, as it will just keep running away from you.

Allow me to give you some tips: 
-learn (from youtube) what drain tanking is. While it's not useful in dungeons, it's great during questing

-always get highest dps wand possible, but try to avoid shadow dmg wands. I'll explain it below

-shadow spell dmg is your best stat to get (well spell dmg is better, but rare during lvling). Check on auction house "of shadow wrath" greens. If you can get it cheap, go for it! 

-warlock is great to fight solo against elites, with one exception. You can't solo elites immune to shadow spells, because you can't cast fear/CoEx on them

-your biggest struggle during lvling are going to be shadow immune enemies. If you have quest that needs you to kill some of those, swap pet to imp, let he fireball few times, go immolate and wand (if not shadow wand). You can start using searing pain when enemy is around 50% of health. It's better to heal imp with health funnel, than get enemy attacking you. 

-30+ lvl there is nice shadowweave set from tailoring, worth getting. Also you are going to get siphon life talent and felstone, your DoTs are going to heal you like crazy. 

-about lvl 30 you can go to scarlet monastery - a lot of great items in that dungeons

-Nice BoE item to look for are "necromancer leggins" 

-have fun! 😉

author: Bones
content:
From itemization standpoint you're right, haste is hard to come by, while leveling I prioritized stamina then int and spell power. There are a few pieces of haste you can pick up but nothing ground breaking. 

Fear I found is pretty reliable here on TWoW. My understanding is that it most likely to break on spell application as opposed to from dot damage. So if the intention is to kill something while it's feared you're best off applying dots then fearing any other spell applications have a chance to break the effect. 

I personally rarely ever had mana issues while leveling. This likely be because I took a slower approach, weaving in life taps and drain life to keep myself topped off throughout a fight.

Summonjutsu - GL <Tremor Totems>
content:
Depends on amount of targets but generally will use wrathstone. Vampirism where you can safely. Want to bridge the 30% pdr so with Soul link, you effectively have 50+%pdr unbuffed.

Searing pain and immo are the primary. Hellfire still seems to win out over RoF even with tick time changes but as long as dps have a brain you should be fine using Rain of Fire if 80 damage from the rank 3 hellfire ticks is to much for heals to tolerate.

1-3 targets, soul fire into immo them all and kill in mark order along with dps, target swapping  occasionally like any other tank.

3+ pulls, unless you have the rank 8 pvp gloves or a paladin using concentration aura, just RoF or Hellfire. The pushback even with 70% and weakness curses can turn a 1.5 into a 2.5 or 3.

Main demon will be the Voidwalker. He will be your off tank, positioner and pull tool. His 10% additional pdr also affects him so he has 50% pdr along with you. 

On bosses this may instead become the imp on passive phase shifted. This is to cut down on health funnel healing draining your health.

Your Felhunter is your most important demon. It can silence/interupt and can remove magic debuffs. This includes a lot of bs silence effects that screw our ability to generate threat.

Speaking of, let's explain the wrathstone (which really needs shadow damage added to it >.> but I get it, 6% hit tank would be busted) All fire damage you deal gets a 40% multiplier. This can go to 60% with the improved stones talent. So for example, if you cast a searing pain that generated 100 threat, it generates 140 or 160 when talented instead.

This includes stuff like imp fire shield, fire wands, sapper charges, oil of immolation, even fiery weapon if you want to try and weave some procs in there between casts. This includes your normal fire spells as well but isn't limited to them.

author: Summonjutsu - GL <Tremor Totems>
content:
So for us it's about stat weights. 

For example hit is worth infinite spell power until you hit the cap of 16/15%+EB. Once you hit the cap, it is worth zero spell power.

Haste and crit work the same way, each 1% of haste is worth around 14-15 spellpower iirc, each 1% crit around 17 spell power.

Depending on your spec these numbers will be different, if you are dark harvest affliction  crit is worth next to 0 spell power since you use mostly channels and dots.

Once you have the value of the stats, you can then look at the gear. Hard white stats like Stam and int do take up parts of the item budget. It's usually better to keep on the lower end for higher green stats and values like crit haste and sp. In general those will be more useful than the hard stats.

Putting it all together let's compare two similar items.

https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=60501

The whip here ^^^ provides 3% haste and some riding speed

https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=18467

The Royal Seal ^^^ provides 23 spell damage and some fire resistance.

For affliction warlocks the whip wins out because 3% haste is valued at around 42-45 spell power over the Royal Seal.

For Destro Warlocks the seal comes out ahead because haste provides no real benefits to searing pain. GCD is still 1.5 seconds we have to wait. 

For Demo the seal comes out ahead mostly because the pet can't inherit any of our haste but it can our spell power and crit so those stats are more highly valued.

author: Summonjutsu - GL <Tremor Totems>
content:
Fro, the best way i can explain why you jump to 2450 tps in that instance is because of the instances of damage being applied in succession. So for every global of the tank you are putting out 4-7 instances of guarenteed damage during harvest. Even though dots dont crit you are putting out 1600 damage a tick. If they glance their white hit, it's likely you are pull agro just from the first machine gun damage instances.

Siphon agony corruption drain soul. They are 30, 24, and 18 sec durations specifically because of the ordering they should be applied to allow the tank to generate threat. Lowest damage ticking longest lasting first. Agony specifically deals it's bigger ticks near the end by design for this purpose.

Honestly throw in a life tap after putting up all the dots  before the drain soul. That way the siphon life healing isn't wasted.
